citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven types of mathematical reasoning and diverse visual contexts including geometry diagrams, charts, natural images, and scientific figures.
name: MathVista
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (each example in the new datasets and VQA labeling was independently annotated by three reviewers/annotators; human performance evaluation used 5 annotators per question)
rai:annotatorDemographics: New dataset annotation: graduate students in STEM fields. VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: expert annotators (details not specified). Human performance evaluation (AMT): annotators required to have a high school diploma or higher, a history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks, and an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial inter-annotator agreement. For the three new datasets: inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 newly collected questions exhibited disagreements). For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation: 94.1% of examples had the exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations; 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tools (GUI shown in Figures 22, 23, 24 of the paper). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for human performance evaluation on the testmini subset.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For VQA dataset labeling: three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using a custom annotation tool with instructions and examples. Annotators chose Yes/No/Unsure. Majority voting was used to finalize labels. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA): all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For mathematical reasoning category labeling: expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven reasoning type candidates using a custom annotation tool.
rai:dataBiases: Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation and avoid over-representation of any single source. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (Chinese and Persian), which may introduce language bias. The benchmark includes problems at varying grade levels (elementary, high school, college), with 30.9% at high-school level and 10.8% at college level, which may bias evaluation toward certain educational contexts. Human performance baseline was restricted to annotators with high school diploma or higher, which may not represent the full population.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected from three sources: (1) Nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (2,666 examples), each limited to up to 400 examples; (2) 19 VQA datasets selected from over 70 reviewed datasets that contain math-related instances and are publicly available (2,739 examples), using heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by expert annotation; (3) Three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) with 736 examples, annotated by graduate students in STEM fields.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) plus newly collected examples. IQTest examples were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA examples involve functional plots. PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/papers).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023. The dataset was published at ICLR 2024 (arXiv submission October 2023).
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains (science, college-level math) makes data collection labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous sources; annotations lack a unified format and structure. The benchmark focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models at time of publication. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (Chinese and Persian), which may affect model evaluation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words (e.g., most, least, mean, average, total, sum, percentage, ratio) were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. The dataset was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets using a sampling strategy to maintain distribution similarity (KL Divergence=0.008, TV distance=0.035).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets (e.g., refining potential data noise) in response to community feedback, and to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista is intended to drive development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. Potential applications include solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights a significant gap (10.4%) between the best AI model (GPT-4V) and human performance, underscoring the need for further AI improvements in mathematical and visual reasoning.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) in visual contexts; benchmarking AI progress on tasks requiring fine-grained visual understanding and compositional reasoning; facilitating development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios; evaluating models across diverse mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, statistical) and visual contexts.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor to extract short answer text from detailed model responses (achieving >99.5% accuracy on 200 examples). EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) was used to detect OCR text from images for augmented LLM evaluation. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLM evaluation. Heuristic rules based on quantity word dictionaries were used for automatic selection of mathematical problems from VQA datasets.
